messages:
anya: quick flag — Cust 'HelionFin' LoRA merge into our staging candidate shows widespread token-substitution after int4 quant. Not typical spm version mismatch.

bryce: short repro?

anya: ran our normal quickpack: `python eval_pack/run_eval.py --pack helion_invoices_180 --model merged_helion_lora --quant int4`

li: what's the symptom? missing tokens or id shifts?

anya: lots of vendor names and short codes turned into adjacent tokens or <unk>. Example: 
INPUT: "Vendor: Helion Labs
Ref: HXN-92"
FP16: "Vendor: Helion Labs"
INT4: "Vendor: Helion <unk>s
Ref: <unk>-92"
Token diff: several tokens appear to have slid by small offsets, but pattern points at some ids removed entirely.

nate: removed entirely? like vocabulary pruning during finetune?

anya: Exactly. Customer finetune pipeline used `--shrink_vocab` to prune low-frequency tokens and produced a LoRA whose tokenizer metadata lists a reduced tokenset. Merge into base (full vocab) reindexes embeddings assuming contiguous ids -> collisions/holes after quant-block packing.

bryce: interesting and different. Remapping will be trickier: we need to expand remap (pruned->base) and patch holes while preserving quant block checksums.

li: two remediations: (A) rebuild LoRA by expanding embedding deltas into base vocab rows (fill pruned rows with zeros) then optionally run `--calibrate` on the affected rows, or (B) retokenize finetune to avoid shrink_vocab and retrain. (A) is faster.

anya: I adapted rebase tool to handle shrink maps: `tools/tokenmap/expand_pruned_lora.py --in lora_helion_pruned.pt --map pruned_to_base.json --out lora_helion_expanded.pt` — it inserts zero-rows for pruned tokens and reindexes. Can @eval-bot run helion_invoices_180 comparing fp16, int4_raw, int4_expanded?

eval-bot: queued 5660004350: helion_invoices_180 on merged_helion fp16, int4_raw, int4_expanded. ETA ~13m. Results and artifacts will be at /runs/5660004350.

nate: note: when expanding, make sure quant-block packing metadata is regenerated because the token->block mapping changes when adding zero rows. Otherwise kernels will read wrong blocks.

bryce: also log the shrink threshold used by the finetune so we can correlate failure modes. Add gating: block merging if LoRA metadata contains shrink_vocab:true without an explicit `--expand-pruned` flag.

anya: pulled interim staging summary: fp16 EM=0.90, int4_raw EM=0.48, int4_expanded EM=0.87. Expansion recovers a lot. Remaining failures (~3%) are tokens that were intentionally aliased in the customer's shrink step (merged multiple rare tokens into a single surrogate). Need a surface-level fallback mapping for those aliases.

li: plan: 1) add `expand_pruned` path in merge pipeline that reconstructs full-vocab LoRA with zero-rows and updates quant-block metadata, 2) add an optional calibration `--calibrate-affected` which runs a small fit over 60 customer samples to nudge alias mappings, 3) add regression checks in helion_invoices_180: EM_drop(fp16 -> int4_expanded_cal) <= 0.05, 4) update SE onboarding note: "if finetune used shrink_vocab, provide pruned_to_base.json or opt into expand_pruned in merge."

anya: I'll open PR with the expand tool, gating logic, repro commands, and the 60-sample adversarial subset capturing surrogate aliases. Will attach run 5660004350 artifacts.

bryce: :thumbsup: add a console warning when uploading LoRA that lists shrink_vocab metadata and recommends expansion or retrain. Also keep the pruned artifact so rollback is possible.

li: I'll add unit tests for expand_pruned to verify quant-blocks and to detect alias collisions.

anya: If anyone wants additional runs (compare expand vs retokenize vs expand+calibrate) I can queue them on staging.
